title: Cairn standard manifest
description: Describes one hosted standard: its identity, upstream source, and the releases/artifacts Cairn replicates and serves.

id.description: URL segment for the standard (must not encode the responsible organisation).

summary.description: One or two sentences for the landing page and catalog.

based_on.description: The source standard this is based on, e.g. 'International Standard for Describing Functions (ISDF), 2007'.

steward.description: The organisation responsible for the standard. Displayed, never part of the URL.

source.description: Default upstream location for artifacts. Individual artifacts may override the ref/path.

links.description: Extra links shown on the landing page (spec home, tag library, mailing list, ...).

major_lines.description: One entry per major version line; 'latest' is what /<id>/vN redirects to.

namespace.description: Optional explicit namespace URI; defaults to https://standards.openpreservation.org/<id>/vMAJOR.

rules.description: Validation-rule revisions published alongside the releases, on their own cadence. Each is served under its major line at /<id>/vN/schematron/<revision>/ and is write-once once published, exactly like a release. They live here rather than inside a release because a published release may never gain an artifact, which would mean a new schema version for every revision of rules that did not change the schema.

then.$comment: A published release pins its own ref so it can be rebuilt from the manifest alone.

ref.description: Git ref for this release; overrides source.ref. Required once lifecycle is 'published', and it should be a tag or commit SHA rather than a branch; cairn cannot verify which it is, so pinning a branch silently gives up rebuildability.

lifecycle.description: Whether the bytes may still change. 'draft' is re-fetched and overwritten every sync; 'published' is write-once forever. Only ever moves draft -> published; the reverse is refused by the PR gate.

served.description: Whether the URLs answer 200 or 410. Freely toggled in both directions; withdrawing a release does not un-publish it.

maturity.description: Display label only. Has no effect on freezing or serving.

then.$comment: A published rules revision pins its own ref so it can be rebuilt from the manifest alone. Same rule as a release, same reason.

revision.description: Dated label for this revision, served at /<id>/vN/schematron/<revision>/. Dated rather than free-form so that 'newest' is decidable by sorting, which is what the moving 'latest' pointer resolves by; it also keeps the word 'latest' out of the revision space so a revision can never shadow the pointer. cairn additionally parses it as a calendar date, so a day that exists only in some months is refused as well.

applies_to.description: The major line these rules validate, matching the namespace URI the .sch file itself declares. Rules are attached to a major line, never to a concrete version, so a new patch release does not require them to be republished.

tested_against.description: The exact release this revision was written and tested against. Only the rules' author knows it, so it is recorded from what they state and displayed beside the checksums; nothing is gated on it. Must name a release of this standard in the same major line.

minimum_version.description: The earliest release in the line these rules apply to, when that is not the whole line. Omit unless a revision genuinely depends on something introduced part-way through the major line. Must name a release of this standard in the same major line, and must not be above tested_against.

ref.description: Git ref for this revision; overrides source.ref. Required once lifecycle is 'published', and it should be a tag or commit SHA rather than a branch; cairn cannot verify which it is, so pinning a branch silently gives up rebuildability.

lifecycle.description: Whether the bytes may still change. 'draft' is re-fetched and overwritten every sync, which is how a revision follows a branch while its rules are still settling; 'published' is write-once forever. Only ever moves draft -> published; the reverse is refused by the PR gate.

served.description: Whether the URLs answer 200 or 410. Freely toggled in both directions; withdrawing a revision does not un-publish it, and the 'latest' pointer skips it.

maturity.description: Display label only. Has no effect on freezing or serving.

name.description: Filename to serve as, under the version folder. Must not begin with a dot, must not be a name cairn generates, and is checked again by cairn with a stricter anchor. JSON Schema patterns are ECMA-262, where \A and \Z are literal letters rather than anchors.

role.description: Drives the RDDL nature and landing-page grouping.

path.description: For from=repo/github-pages: path within the repo/site.

asset.description: For from=release-asset: asset filename or glob within the GitHub Release.

release_tag.description: For from=release-asset: the GitHub Release tag (defaults to the release ref).

media_type.description: Override the served Content-Type (else inferred from extension).

title.description: Human label for the landing page / RDDL.
